sources: Joint Maritime Information Centre (JMIC) Update 111 Advisory Note, Nov 5, 2026, distributed by UKMTO (T1); relayed by Gulf News (T3)
fault_line: Counted attacks vs claimed fires -- JMIC counts 4 attacks in 4 days, the IRGC claims 5 tankers on fire: is Iran really hitting ships, or staging fires for leverage while the strait stays shut?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE DATA -- JMIC Update 111, Nov 5, via UKMTO, relayed by Gulf News] Four attacks in the Strait of Hormuz over 96 hours (Nov 1-3), up from three in the preceding reporting period; all four occurred within ~52 hours off Oman's Musandam coast. IRGC activity continued: UAV overflights, targeted surveillance and occasional VHF radio hailing of merchant shipping. The Arabian Gulf recorded two attacks in the period, bringing the area total to eight since October 7; one incident (UKMTO 196-26) was a tanker struck by two unidentified projectiles ~50nm north of Qatar (Nov 4, 23:20 UTC), crew/damage unconfirmed, no claim of responsibility. Commercial vessel movements through Hormuz remained 'substantially reduced' vs pre-conflict levels. US NCAGS data: ~31 US-assisted transits/day in the reporting period, slightly below the 34/day average of Oct 24-30. CENTCOM figures dated Nov 1: 144 commercial vessels redirected, 4 disabled during blockade enforcement, 2 boarded for compliance checks. [CORROBORATING CONTEXT -- Reuters (T1 wire) via Dawn/GMA relays, Nov 5] At least five vessels reported incidents since Sunday; October saw 35 vessels hit, the most of any month of the war; most crews now decline to report strikes. [PORTWATCH -- STALE, DO NOT CITE AS CURRENT] Newest snapshot portwatch-2026-10-26.json is STALE (latest observation 2026-10-18: Hormuz 4 transits, 7-day avg 3.71 vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day = 4.3%). The JMIC Nov 1-5 counts are the current counted figures; the Oct 18 PortWatch count is NOT current and is never substituted for the JMIC figures.
sections.what_verified: 3 tiered families: JMIC/UKMTO (T1, primary source of the advisory) + Gulf News (T3, relay) + Reuters (T1 wire, Qatar strike / 5-since-Sunday / 35-in-October figures via Dawn and GMA relays). Counts are JMIC's own tracked data, not a claimant figure.
sections.what_disputed: IRGC claims (Operational Statement 21, Nov 5, via Sepah News/IRIB) that five tankers + one tugboat caught fire after striking mines on 'unauthorised routes' -- UNVERIFIED: no vessel names, flags or casualty details; overlap with the four JMIC-counted attacks is unclear; AP notes the claims have not been independently verified. IRGC also claims capture of two US LUCAS drones -- unverified, no US/CENTCOM confirmation. The ~31/day figure is US-ASSISTED transits (NCAGS), not total transits; JMIC gives no total-transit count and no JMIC-stated pre-conflict daily figure (do not substitute the PortWatch 2025 mean 85.53/day as JMIC's baseline -- different scope, and stale). The Qatar tanker (UKMTO 196-26) attacker is unidentified.
sections.why_matters: Counted, not claimed: 4 attacks in 96 hours off Musandam -- and only about 31 US-assisted ships a day are getting through Hormuz while CENTCOM has redirected 144 vessels.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Gulf News published 05:36 , 05:00-06:00 window; not recorded at 0600; 0800-02 covered only the Bab al-Mandeb section of the same advisory) -- JMIC Update 111: Hormuz attacks rise to 4 in 96 hours; US-assisted transits ~31/day; CENTCOM Nov 1 figures

totw_analysis: Our read: Counted, not claimed: 4 attacks in 96 hours off Musandam -- and only about 31 US-assisted ships a day are getting through Hormuz while CENTCOM has redirected 144 vessels. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Counted attacks vs claimed fires -- JMIC counts 4 attacks in 4 days, the IRGC claims 5 tankers on fire: is Iran really hitting ships, or staging fires for leverage while the strait stays shut?
